Unfortunately, unforeseen complications involving the Brownfield Cleanup Program (BCP) required us to reevaluate our approach and pivot from our previous plans. The wetland system on site is an area worthy of protection. The Applicant recognizes this, and the project has been designed to avoid fully any new disturbance to the onsite wetland and minimal disturbance to the wetland buffer area. There is limited disturbance within the onsite wetland buffer only. The proposed project involves construction of a self-storage facility building and re-shaping of the existing detention basin. The proposed areas of disturbance are associated with a developed and operational site. Upon completion of the proposed work the areas of disturbance within the Wetland Buffer will be stabilized. There will be no physical disturbance to the wetland area and the area of disturbance within the wetland buffer will be protected with erosion control measures such as silt fencing and orange construction fencing. All erosion control measures shall remain in place until there is a vegetative cover of at least 80% coverage in the disturbed areas. The project would maintain the integrity of the natural habitat as much as possible and any potential impacts to the wetland system because of the proposed project would be minimal. Page 2 | Town Clerk: (585) 340-8629 | clerk@penfield.org | www.penfield.org PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-164 DATE: November 4, 2026 BY Councilperson Getz Law and Finance Committee NAME Budget Transfers for the General Fund WHEREAS, the Town Board desires to have an up-to-date budget in relation to current income and expenditures, NOW, BE IT RESOLVED, that the following 2026 budget transfers be approved: Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry Dean Getz Lang Teglash ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T- 165 DATE: November 4, 2026 BY: Councilperson Getz Law & Finance Committee NAME: Express the Town Board’s intention for completion of real property revaluations every four years, beginning in 2028 WHEREAS, the Town of Penfield recognizes the importance of maintaining accurate and equitable assessments of real property to promote fairness in the distribution of the property tax burden; and WHEREAS, regular revaluations help ensure that assessments reflect changes in market values and that property owners are treated equitably in accordance with applicable New York State law; and WHEREAS, establishing a consistent revaluation schedule provides greater predictability for property owners and supports responsible municipal planning and budgeting; and WHEREAS, the Town Board believes that completing a townwide real property revaluation every four years is a reasonable and appropriate goal for maintaining equitable assessments; and WHEREAS, the Town Board intends to establish 2028 as the starting year for this fouryear revaluation cycle, with subsequent revaluations intended for 2032, 2036, and every four years thereafter; and WHEREAS, New York State offers Aid for Cyclical Reassessments to qualifying municipalities that commit to an approved recurring reassessment program; and WHEREAS, the Town Assessor agrees with the Town Board on these matters, NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penfield hereby expresses its intention that townwide real property revaluations be completed every four years, beginning in 2028 and continuing on a four-year cycle thereafter; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Board intends to work with the Town Assessor and other appropriate officials to plan and implement this schedule, subject to applicable law, available resources, and the adoption of necessary annual budgets and appropriations; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Board recognizes the importance of communicating the revaluation schedule to residents and providing appropriate public information regarding the assessment process and its implications for individual property owners. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-166__ BY: Councilperson Getz DATE: November 4, 2027 COMMITTEE: Law & Finance NAME: Authorize the Supervisor to sign a Lease Agreement with the Eastside Area Annex WHEREAS, the Town of Penfield desires to continue its Lease Agreement with the Eastside Area Annex for the provision of office and meeting space; and NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Supervisor is hereby authorized to execute a Lease Agreement with the Eastside Area Annex for office and meeting space located in the Don Mack Building, 1587 Jackson Road, for a term commencing January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2032, subject to review and approval by the Town Attorney. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-167 BY: Councilperson Getz DATE:__November 4 , 2026 COMMITTEE: Law and Finance NAME Adopt a Local Law to Amend Town Code Section 22-7 (Ethics Board Membership) WHEREAS, a proposed local law was introduced in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A, which would amend Section 22-7 (Establishment; membership) of Article III (Board of Ethics) of Chapter 22 (Code of Ethics) of the Code of the Town of Penfield to increase the number of members from five (5) to seven (7) (the “Proposed Law”), a copy of which is attached hereto as Schedule A; and WHEREAS, pursuant to Municipal Home Rule § 20(5) no local law shall be passed by the Town Board until a public hearing is held; and WHEREAS, a public hearing was scheduled for September 2, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.; and WHEREAS, notice of said public hearing was duly published in the official newspaper of the Town and posted as required by law; and WHEREAS, a public hearing was held on September 2, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.to hear all persons interested in the Proposed Local Law; and WHEREAS, the Town Board received a written copy of the Proposed Law at least ten (10) days before this meeting (excluding Sundays), pursuant to Municipal Home Rule § 20(4); and WHEREAS, The Town Board, after due deliberation, finds it in the best interest of the Town of Penfield to adopt this Proposed Law. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that pursuant to the New York State Environmental Quality Review Act and its enabling regulations (collectively “SEQRA”), the enactment of the Proposed Law is classified as a Type II Action pursuant to 6 NYCRR §§ 617.7(c)(33) (“adoption of regulations, policies, procedures and local legislative decisions in connection with any action on this list”) and 617.7(c)(26) (“routine or continuing agency administration and management, not including new programs or major reordering of priorities that may affect the environment”), and therefore the Town Board determines that further environmental review pursuant to SEQRA is not required. AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED AND BE IT ENACTED BY THE TOWN BOARD OF THE TOWN OF PENFIELD, the Proposed Law, which will be referred to as Local Law No. 8 of 2026, a Local Law to amend 22-7 of the Code of the Town of Penfield, a copy of which is attached hereto and made a part hereof as Schedule A. AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, after its adoption by the Town Board of the Town of Penfield, this local law shall take effect immediately upon its filing with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of New York. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-168 BY: Councilperson Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 COMMITTEE: Law and Finance NAME: Adopt a Local Law to Amend Town Code Section 250-13.12 (Cannabis Retail Dispensary) WHEREAS, a proposed local law was introduced in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A, which would amend Section 250-13.12 of Article XIII (Conditional Use Permits) of Chapter 250 (Zoning) of the Code of the Town of Penfield to modify the Town’s Conditional Use Permit requirements to ensure compliance with the New York Cannabis Law and to allow cannabis retail dispensaries as conditionally permitted uses in the Limited Business District (the “Proposed Law”), a copy of which is attached hereto as Schedule A; and WHEREAS, pursuant to Municipal Home Rule § 20(5) no local law shall be passed by the Town Board until a public hearing is held; and WHEREAS, a public hearing was scheduled for October 4, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.; an WHEREAS, notice of said public hearing was duly published in the official newspaper of the Town and posted as required by law; and WHEREAS, a public hearing was held on October 4, 2026, at 6:30 p.m.to hear all persons interested in the Proposed Local Law; and WHEREAS, the Town Board received a written copy of the Proposed Law at least ten (10) days before this meeting (excluding Sundays), pursuant to Municipal Home Rule § 20(4); and WHEREAS, The Town Board, after due deliberation, finds it in the best interest of the Town of Irondequoit to adopt this Proposed Law. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that pursuant to the New York State Environmental Quality Review Act and its enabling regulations (collectively “SEQRA”), the enactment of the Proposed Law is classified as a Type II Action pursuant to 6 NYCRR §§ 617.7(c)(33) (“adoption of regulations, policies, procedures and local legislative decisions in connection with any action on this list”) and 617.7(c)(26) (“routine or continuing agency administration and management, not including new programs or major reordering of priorities that may affect the environment”), and therefore the Town Board determines that further environmental review pursuant to SEQRA is not required. AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED AND BE IT ENACTED BY THE TOWN BOARD OF THE TOWN OF PENFIELD, the Proposed Law, which will be referred to as Local Law No. 8 of 2026, a Local Law to amend section 25-13.12 of the Code of the Town of Penfield, a copy of which is attached hereto and made a part hereof as Schedule A. AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, after its adoption by the Town Board of the Town of Penfield, this local law shall take effect immediately upon its filing with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of New York. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the Penfield Town Board acknowledges the completion of the analysis, accepts the final Fiscal Impact Analysis and Housing Study, and thanks the RKG Associates team for their work on the project. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-170 BY: Councilperson Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 Law and Finance Committee NAME: Adoption of the Town of Penfield 2027 Fee Schedule WHEREAS, the Town Board is authorized to set and amend fees from time to time; and WHEREAS, Town staff identified some minor additions and changes to ensure the fee schedule is consistent with departmental operations, which are included in the attached 2027 fee schedule. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the Town Board approves the 2027 fee schedule, which shall be in effect beginning January 1, 2026. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-171___ BY Councilperson_Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 COMMITTEE:_Law & Finance NAME : To Adopt the Children and Youth Protection and Abuse Prevention Policy WHEREAS, the Town of Penﬁeld is committed to maintaining a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for all individuals involved in its recreation programs, and activities; WHEREAS, sexual abuse and misconduct, including but not limited to inappropriate physical conduct, exploitation, and assault, are serious violations of human dignity and legal standards and must be proactively prevented; WHEREAS, the Town of Penﬁeld recognizes its ethical and legal responsibility to take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual abuse and misconduct, respond appropriately to any allegations, and to support affected individuals; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penﬁeld, hereby adopts the Children and Youth Protection and Abuse Prevention Policy; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town of Penﬁeld directs its staff to implement the Children and Youth Protection and Abuse Prevention Policy. (CSEA) have negotiated employment terms in good faith in order to ﬁnalize a successor agreement; WHEREAS; as a result of negotiations, both parties reached and agreed to a tentative agreement effective January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2029; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby authorizes the Town Supervisor to sign a collective bargaining agreement between the Town and the Civil Service Employees Association, Inc., pending Town Attorney and counsel to the Town Attorney approval, and ratiﬁcation by CSEA membership vote. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean___ Getz___ Lang___ Teglash___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-173___ BY Councilperson_Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 COMMITTEE:_Law & Finance NAME: Authorization to Approve the Inclusion of Sewer Department Employees in existing CSEA Bargaining Unit WHEREAS, the Town of Penﬁeld currently recognizes the Civil Service Employees Association (CSEA) as the collective bargaining representative for eligible employees of the Highway Department within the Department of Public Works; and WHEREAS, CSEA has organized eligible employees of the Town of Penﬁeld Sewer Department for the purpose of collective bargaining representation; and WHEREAS, representatives of the Town of Penﬁeld and CSEA have agreed upon a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) providing for the inclusion of eligible Sewer Department employees in the existing CSEA bargaining unit; and WHEREAS, the Town Board recognizes the agreement reached between the parties and desires to formally approve the expansion of the existing bargaining unit to include eligible Sewer Department employees; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penﬁeld hereby approves and ratiﬁes the Memorandum of Agreement between the Town of Penﬁeld and CSEA providing for the inclusion of eligible Sewer Department employees in the existing CSEA bargaining unit; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that eligible Sewer Department employees shall be included in the existing CSEA bargaining unit in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the Memorandum of Agreement; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Supervisor and appropriate Town officials are hereby authorized and directed to take all necessary actions to implement the terms of the Memorandum of Agreement. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean___ Getz___ Lang___ Teglash___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-174 BY: Councilperson Lang DATE: Nov. 4, 2026 Public Works Committee NAME: Establishing the Clark Barn Beam Advisory Committee WHEREAS, the Penfield Town Board owns a parcel located at 1960 Clark Road which formerly included a barn; and WHEREAS, the barn has been demolished and, under the direction of the Town Supervisor, the Department of Public Works retained and stored all usable beams, 42 in total; and WHEREAS, the Town Board desires more information and input to make its determination regarding the most appropriate future use for the beams; and WHEREAS, the Penfield Town Board wishes to formulate a Clark Barn Beam Advisory Committee (the “Advisory Committee”) to provide input and recommendations related to the future actions pertaining to the beams, including possible use in a project(s) of historical and/or cultural significance to the town; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board approves the immediate formation of the Advisory Committee, which shall include representatives from relevant town departments, boards and committees, town residents and property owners; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Supervisor shall take immediate steps to identify potential Advisory Committee members, including public outreach to interested town residents and property owners; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Advisory Committee shall commence its activities as soon as committee membership has been approved by the Town Board. title: November 23, 2026 | Special/Emergency Meeting - Ordinance 16.101.26
text: COMMON COUNCIL CITY OF ALBANY, NEW YORK SPECIAL/EMERGENCY MEETING Notice is hereby given that there will be a special/emergency meeting of the Albany Common Council at the following days and time: • Monday, November 23, 2026 at 5:30pm • Monday, November 30, 2026 at 5:30pm The meetings will take place in the Common Council Chambers on the second floor of City Hall. No other business other than the consideration of the below ordinance will be conducted: Ordinance 16.101.26 AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING THE CITY OF ALBANY BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027 AS PRESENTED BY THE MAYOR ON OCTOBER 1, 2026 There will be a period for public comment. Kelly Kimbrough Common Council President This notice and the included ordinance may be subject to revisions. The Albany Common Council encourages members of the public to provide public comment in-person or online. To provide in-person commentary, one can show up before the meeting to sign up, or use the link that follows 30 minutes prior to the meeting. One can also email commoncouncil@albanyny.gov to provide written public comment, or use the same link that follows: https://albanyny.gov/FormCenter/Common-Council-15/Online-Public-Comment-SignUpSubmission-F-59 Council Member Keegan, on behalf of the Committee on Finance, Assessment and Taxation, introduced the following: ORDINANCE 16.101.26 AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING THE CITY OF ALBANY BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027 AS PRESENTED BY THE MAYOR ON OCTOBER 1, 2026 The City of Albany, in Common Council convened, does hereby ordain and enact: Section 1. The 2027 City Budget as proposed by the Mayor on October 1, 2026 is hereby adopted as the Budget of the City of Albany for fiscal year 2027. Section 2. It is hereby ordered and directed that the sums set forth therein as expenditures are hereby appropriated in the amounts and for the several departments, offices and purposes specified therein under the following general categories of expenditure: Personal Services (Code 10); Equipment (Code 20); Contractual Expenditures (Code 40); Debt Principal (Code 60); Debt Interest (Code 70); Employee Benefits (Code 80); Inter-fund Transfers (Code 90); and Capital Projects. Section 3. It is further hereby ordered and directed that the positions set forth therein are hereby authorized, created, and/or continued. The number appearing on the line items of each position shall be the number of positions under such title. Salary grades as proposed by the Mayor are hereby adopted and incorporated. Section 4. It is further hereby ordered and directed that any changes to an individual salary of an employee at Grade 7 and above, that is more than ten (10) percent of the planned rate as presented by the Budget Director for any position within the several departments, offices, and commissions for the fiscal year requires consent of the Common Council as dictated in section 604 of the Charter of the City of Albany. Section 5. It is further hereby ordered and directed that any changes to an individual salary of an employee at Grade 6 and below, that is more than twenty (20) percent of the planned rate as presented by the Budget Director of any position within the several departments, offices, and commissions for the fiscal year requires consent of the Common Council as dictated in Section 604, Article VI (Finance) of the Charter of the City of Albany. Section 6. It is further hereby directed that, notwithstanding any provision of local law to the contrary, the City Treasurer may authorize the temporary use of US Treasury Local Fiscal Recovery Funds on account with the City which are not immediately required for the purpose or purposes for which they have been authorized. Such funds shall be made again available to the City in accordance with applicable provisions New York State General Municipal and Local Finance Law, and City Code. Section 7. It is further hereby ordered and directed that the sums set forth in the budget as presented by the Mayor on October 1, 2026 as revenues and moneys necessary to be raised by tax in addition thereto, to pay the expenses of conducting the business of the City, shall be and are hereby applicable in the amounts specified for the purpose of meeting said appropriations. Section 8. The ordinance shall take effect immediately. APPROVED AS TO FORM THIS 24TH DAY OF SEPTEMBER, 2026 ___ CORPORATION COUNSEL To: Shaniqua Jackson, City Clerk From: Martha Mahoney, Esq., Senior Assistant Corporation Counsel Re: Common Council Legislation Supporting Memorandum Date: September 24, 2026 Sponsor: Council Member Keegan, on behalf of the Committee on Finance, Assessment and Taxation ORDINANCE 16.101.26 (MC) TITLE AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING THE CITY OF ALBANY BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2027 AS PRESENTED BY THE MAYOR ON OCTOBER 1, 2026 GENERAL PURPOSE OF LEGISLATION To adopt the budget for the City for the 2027 fiscal year. NECESSITY FOR LEGISLATIONA ND ANY CHANGE TO EXISTING LAW Under the City Charter, the Common Council must adopt the budget, with or without amendments, on or before November 30. FISCAL IMPACTS This ordinance approves the City budget for 2027.

TOWN OF MARCELLUS LOCAL LAW NO. 2 OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO AMEND THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS ZONING LAW TO ADD A NEW SECTION REGARDING STEEP SLOPE PROTECTIONS BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Marcellus as follows: SECTION 1 AUTHORITY. This local law is enacted pursuant to the New York State Constitution and New York Municipal Home Rule Law § 10. SECTION 2 AMENDMENTS TO THE TOWN OF MARCELLUS ZONING LAW TO ADD A NEW SECTION 235-26.2 (“STEEP SLOPE PROTECTIONS”). The Town of Marcellus Zoning Law is hereby amended to add Section 235-26.2 as follows: “(1) Purpose The purpose of this Steep Slope Protection Law is to conserve the sensitive environment of steep slope areas, and to regulate land use within these areas in a manner which protects the public interest by minimizing detrimental effects of land disturbance and development on steep slopes by: A.Providing for the reasonable use of steep slopes while ensuring development will not induce soil erosion, unreasonably alter the natural topography of the area, require excessive grading, increase slope instability, increase stormwater runoff, contaminate surface waters, or create onsite sewage treatment problems. B. Guarding against property damage and personal injury. C.Minimizing the potential for erosion, slope failure, stream siltation, increased stormwater runoff, flooding, contamination of surface waters; and protecting the water quality of Nine Mile Creek, Otisco Lake, and other downstream bodies of water. D.Conserving existing steep slope woodlands for air and water quality benefits and the preservation of wildlife habitats. (2) Definitions. CLEARING: Removing or causing to be removed the vegetation growing in the soil which protects and stabilizes the soil. Such removing or causing to be removed shall include any intentional or negligent act to (1) cut down, (2) remove all or a substantial part of, or (3) damage a tree or other vegetation which will cause the tree or other vegetation to decline and/or die. Such acts shall include but not be limited to damage inflicted upon the root system of the vegetation by the application of toxic substances, by the operation of equipment and vehicles, by storage of materials, or by the damage of natural grade due to unapproved excavation or filling, or damage caused by the unapproved alteration of natural physical conditions. The area of land disturbance of a mature tree shall be measured as the crown of the tree. LAND DISTURBANCE: Any man-made change to the land surface that may result in soil erosion from water or wind and the movement of sediments into a Watercourse, including, but not limited to, clearing, grading, excavating, transporting, and filling of land, paving of existing pervious areas or otherwise creating new impervious areas. WATERCOURSE: Every spring, pond (other than artificial reservoirs and filter basins}, stream, creek, lake, ditch, gutter, or other channel of every kind, the waters of which will run whether continuously or occasionally. (3) Steep slope protection areas (SSPA) A. The steep slope protection areas shall include all lands having slopes 15% or greater. B. Steep slope protection areas are further categorized as: (1) Moderately steep: 15% to less than 24.9% slope (3 to 6 in 12); (2) Very steep: 25% to less than 49.9% slope (6 to 10 in 12); and (3) Extremely steep: 50% or greater slope (> 10 in 12). (4) (5) G The Town of Marcellus Steep Slopes map created, and as may later be amended, by the Syracuse - Onondaga County Planning Agency, the current version of which is attached hereto and incorporated herein as Exhibit “A”, shall be accepted as preliminary evidence of slope. Other scientific or reliable evidence may also be accepted as evidence of steep slope in the sole discretion of the Planning Board. D. The regulations applicable to Steep Slope Protection Areas shall be in addition to and take precedence over the zoning regulations otherwise applicable in each zoning district. Activities within a steep slope protection area requiring site plan review A.The following activities require site plan approval through the Town of Marcellus Planning Board, pursuant to Section 235-28, when located in a steep slope protection area. (1) Area Al: 1000 square feet or greater of land disturbance on a Moderately Steep Slope within 100 feet horizontal distance from any watercourse. (2) Area A2: 500 square feet or greater of land disturbance on a Very Steep or Extremely Steep Slope within 100 feet horizontal distance from any watercourse. (3) Area B: 3000 square feet or greater of land disturbance occurring on a Moderately Steep Slope beyond 100 horizontal feet from any watercourse. (4) Area C: 2000 square feet or greater of land disturbance occurring ona Very Steep or Extremely Steep Slope outside a Lake District and beyond 100 horizontal feet from any watercourse. B.Farming Operations, other than Timber Harvesting, existing as of the effective date of this Article are exempt from the site plan approval required for steep slope protection areas. C.All land disturbance that occurs on the steep slope protection area portion of the parcel (1) within two years or (2) that adjoins and adds to a previous area of disturbance (such as an extension of a driveway) shall be used to calculate the total area of land disturbance. D.Absent approval from the Planning Board, land disturbance ina steep slope protection area that exceeds the square foot limitations set forth above is prohibited. General regulations A.Any development proposed in a steep slope protection area shall be designed to work with the natural elements of the site, locating the proposed improvements in such a manner as to minimize land disturbance, cut and fill operations, tree removal, and alterations to natural drainage. The applicant must provide the Town Planning Board with documentation that the improvements were designed to fit the existing natural elements of the site, rather than making the site fit the development goals of the landowner as part of the site plan review process. Page 2 | Town Clerk: (585) 340-8629 | clerk@penfield.org | www.penfield.org PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-164 DATE: November 4, 2026 BY Councilperson Getz Law and Finance Committee NAME Budget Transfers for the General Fund WHEREAS, the Town Board desires to have an up-to-date budget in relation to current income and expenditures, NOW, BE IT RESOLVED, that the following 2026 budget transfers be approved: Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry Dean Getz Lang Teglash ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T- 165 DATE: November 4, 2026 BY: Councilperson Getz Law & Finance Committee NAME: Express the Town Board’s intention for completion of real property revaluations every four years, beginning in 2028 WHEREAS, the Town of Penfield recognizes the importance of maintaining accurate and equitable assessments of real property to promote fairness in the distribution of the property tax burden; and WHEREAS, regular revaluations help ensure that assessments reflect changes in market values and that property owners are treated equitably in accordance with applicable New York State law; and WHEREAS, establishing a consistent revaluation schedule provides greater predictability for property owners and supports responsible municipal planning and budgeting; and WHEREAS, the Town Board believes that completing a townwide real property revaluation every four years is a reasonable and appropriate goal for maintaining equitable assessments; and WHEREAS, the Town Board intends to establish 2028 as the starting year for this fouryear revaluation cycle, with subsequent revaluations intended for 2032, 2036, and every four years thereafter; and WHEREAS, New York State offers Aid for Cyclical Reassessments to qualifying municipalities that commit to an approved recurring reassessment program; and WHEREAS, the Town Assessor agrees with the Town Board on these matters, NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penfield hereby expresses its intention that townwide real property revaluations be completed every four years, beginning in 2028 and continuing on a four-year cycle thereafter; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Board intends to work with the Town Assessor and other appropriate officials to plan and implement this schedule, subject to applicable law, available resources, and the adoption of necessary annual budgets and appropriations; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Board recognizes the importance of communicating the revaluation schedule to residents and providing appropriate public information regarding the assessment process and its implications for individual property owners. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, the Penfield Town Board acknowledges the completion of the analysis, accepts the final Fiscal Impact Analysis and Housing Study, and thanks the RKG Associates team for their work on the project. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-170 BY: Councilperson Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 Law and Finance Committee NAME: Adoption of the Town of Penfield 2027 Fee Schedule WHEREAS, the Town Board is authorized to set and amend fees from time to time; and WHEREAS, Town staff identified some minor additions and changes to ensure the fee schedule is consistent with departmental operations, which are included in the attached 2027 fee schedule. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the Town Board approves the 2027 fee schedule, which shall be in effect beginning January 1, 2026. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean ___ Getz ___ Lang ___ Teglash ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-171___ BY Councilperson_Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 COMMITTEE:_Law & Finance NAME : To Adopt the Children and Youth Protection and Abuse Prevention Policy WHEREAS, the Town of Penﬁeld is committed to maintaining a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for all individuals involved in its recreation programs, and activities; WHEREAS, sexual abuse and misconduct, including but not limited to inappropriate physical conduct, exploitation, and assault, are serious violations of human dignity and legal standards and must be proactively prevented; WHEREAS, the Town of Penﬁeld recognizes its ethical and legal responsibility to take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual abuse and misconduct, respond appropriately to any allegations, and to support affected individuals; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penﬁeld, hereby adopts the Children and Youth Protection and Abuse Prevention Policy; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town of Penﬁeld directs its staff to implement the Children and Youth Protection and Abuse Prevention Policy. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean___ Getz___ Lang___ Teglash___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-172___ BY Councilperson Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 COMMITTEE: Law & Finance NAME Authorization for Supervisor to sign a Collective Bargaining Agreement WHEREAS; the Town and the Civil Service Employees Association, Inc. (CSEA) have negotiated employment terms in good faith in order to ﬁnalize a successor agreement; WHEREAS; as a result of negotiations, both parties reached and agreed to a tentative agreement effective January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2029; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby authorizes the Town Supervisor to sign a collective bargaining agreement between the Town and the Civil Service Employees Association, Inc., pending Town Attorney and counsel to the Town Attorney approval, and ratiﬁcation by CSEA membership vote. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean___ Getz___ Lang___ Teglash___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-173___ BY Councilperson_Getz DATE: November 4, 2026 COMMITTEE:_Law & Finance NAME: Authorization to Approve the Inclusion of Sewer Department Employees in existing CSEA Bargaining Unit WHEREAS, the Town of Penﬁeld currently recognizes the Civil Service Employees Association (CSEA) as the collective bargaining representative for eligible employees of the Highway Department within the Department of Public Works; and WHEREAS, CSEA has organized eligible employees of the Town of Penﬁeld Sewer Department for the purpose of collective bargaining representation; and WHEREAS, representatives of the Town of Penﬁeld and CSEA have agreed upon a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) providing for the inclusion of eligible Sewer Department employees in the existing CSEA bargaining unit; and WHEREAS, the Town Board recognizes the agreement reached between the parties and desires to formally approve the expansion of the existing bargaining unit to include eligible Sewer Department employees; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penﬁeld hereby approves and ratiﬁes the Memorandum of Agreement between the Town of Penﬁeld and CSEA providing for the inclusion of eligible Sewer Department employees in the existing CSEA bargaining unit; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that eligible Sewer Department employees shall be included in the existing CSEA bargaining unit in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth in the Memorandum of Agreement; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Supervisor and appropriate Town officials are hereby authorized and directed to take all necessary actions to implement the terms of the Memorandum of Agreement. Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry ___ Dean___ Getz___ Lang___ Teglash___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-174 BY: Councilperson Lang DATE: Nov. 4, 2026 Public Works Committee NAME: Establishing the Clark Barn Beam Advisory Committee WHEREAS, the Penfield Town Board owns a parcel located at 1960 Clark Road which formerly included a barn; and WHEREAS, the barn has been demolished and, under the direction of the Town Supervisor, the Department of Public Works retained and stored all usable beams, 42 in total; and WHEREAS, the Town Board desires more information and input to make its determination regarding the most appropriate future use for the beams; and WHEREAS, the Penfield Town Board wishes to formulate a Clark Barn Beam Advisory Committee (the “Advisory Committee”) to provide input and recommendations related to the future actions pertaining to the beams, including possible use in a project(s) of historical and/or cultural significance to the town; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board approves the immediate formation of the Advisory Committee, which shall include representatives from relevant town departments, boards and committees, town residents and property owners; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Supervisor shall take immediate steps to identify potential Advisory Committee members, including public outreach to interested town residents and property owners; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Advisory Committee shall commence its activities as soon as committee membership has been approved by the Town Board. Erin Trostle, Town Clerk Dated at Pound Ridge, New York October 28, 2026 TOWN OF POUND RIDGE LOCAL LAW No. 5 of 2026 A LOCAL LAW to grant a partial real property tax exemption for Active Duty Members of the Armed Forces Serving in a Combat Zone BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Pound Ridge as follows: Section 1. Title. This local law shall be known as “A Local Law to Grant a Partial Real Property Tax Exemption for Active Duty Members of the Armed Forces Serving in a Combat Zone” Section 2. Purpose. The purpose of this local law is to grant a partial exemption of the assessed valuation of real property owned as a primary residence by a member of the armed forces serving in a combat zone as set forth by the Real Property Tax Law of the State of New York, §458-d. All terms, definitions, and conditions of such statute shall apply to this local law. Section 3. Exemption Pursuant to §458-d of the Real Property Tax Law, as added by Chapter 677 of the Laws of 2025, qualifying residential real property owned by an active duty military service member whose military duty station is within New York State and who at any time during the taxable year performed active duty in a combat zone shall be exempt from taxation by the Town of Pound Ridge to the extent of twenty-five percent (25%) of the assessed value of such property; provided, however, that such exemption shall not exceed $20,000 or the product of $20,000 multiplied by the latest state equalization rate for the assessing unit, or in the case of a special assessing unit, the latest class ratio, whichever is less. The exemption provided by the section shall not be applicable to taxes levied for school purposes. If an active military service member is currently receiving an exemption under Section 458, 458-a, or 458-b of the Real Property Tax Law in any given taxable year, the active duty service member shall not be eligible to receive the exemption under this section during the same taxable year. Application for exemption shall be made by the owner, or all of the owners, of the property on a form prescribed by the state board. The owner or owners shall file the completed form in the assessor’s office on or before the first appropriate taxable status date, along with documentation of active duty in a combat zone, such as a copy of military orders or a certified letter from the commanding officer. The owner or owners of the property shall be required to refile each year on or before the appropriate taxable status date. Any applicant convicted of willfully making any false statement in the application for such exemption shall be subject to the penalties prescribed in the Penal Law. Section 4. Severability. If any clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law shall be adjudged by and court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to said clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law. Section 5. Effective Date. This local law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the office of the Secretary of State in accordance with Municipal Home Rule Law §27. TOWN OF POUND RIDGE LOCAL LAW NO. 4 of 2026 A LOCAL LAW to adopt the optional full real property tax exemption for seriously disabled veterans authorized by Real Property Tax Law §458-a(11) BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Pound Ridge as follows: Section 1. Title. This local law shall be known as “A Local Law to Adopt the Optional Full Real Property Tax Exemption for Seriously Disabled Veterans authorized by Real Property Tax Law §458-a(11).” Section 2. Purpose. The purpose of this local law to create an additional alternative veterans exemption for seriously disabled veterans, as set forth by the Real Property Tax Law of the State of New York, §458-a(11). All terms, definitions, and conditions of such statute shall apply to this local law. Section 3. Eligibility. Pursuant to §458-a(11) of the Real Property Tax Law of the State of New York, the veterans eligible to receive the exemption as set forth in that section shall be eligible for same in the Town of Pound Ridge. Section 4. Severability. If any clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law shall be adjudged by and court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to said clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law. Section 5. Effective Date. This local law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the office of the Secretary of State in accordance with Municipal Home Rule Law §27. TOWN OF POUND RIDGE LOCAL LAW No. 6 of 2026 A LOCAL LAW to grant a partial real property tax exemption for surviving spouses of volunteer firefighters and volunteer ambulance service members BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Pound Ridge as follows: Section 1. Title. This local law shall be known as “A Local Law to Grant a Partial Real Property Tax Exemption for Surviving Spouses of Volunteer Firefighters and Volunteer Ambulance Service Members.” Section 2. Purpose. The purpose of this local law to provide volunteer firefighters and volunteer ambulance service members who are qualified real property owners with the tax exemption authorized by §466-a of the Real Property Tax Law and to continue this exemption in the case of certain surviving spouses of deceased volunteers pursuant to that law. The exemptions authorized by this local law are subject to all the qualifications and limitations set forth in §466-a and §466-l of the Real Property Tax Law. Section 3. Exemption Real property owned by the surviving spouse of a deceased member of an incorporated volunteer fire company, fire department, or incorporated voluntary ambulance service killed in the line of duty shall be exempt from taxation to the extent of fifty percent of the assessed value of such property for county purposes and county special district purposes other than sewer purposes, exclusive of special assessments; provided that: A. Such surviving spouse is certified by the authority having jurisdiction for the incorporated volunteer fire company, fire department, or incorporated voluntary ambulance service as surviving spouse of an enrolled member of such incorporated volunteer fire company, fire department, or incorporated voluntary ambulance service who was killed in the line of duty; and B. Such deceased volunteer had been an enrolled member for at least five years; and C. Such deceased volunteer had been receiving an exemption prior to their death. Section 4. Severability. If any clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law shall be adjudged by and court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to said clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law. Section 5. Effective date. This local law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the office of the Secretary of State in accordance with Municipal Home Rule Law §27. TOWN OF POUND RIDGE LOCAL LAW No. 7 of 2026 A LOCAL LAW to grant a Partial Real Property Tax Exemption for Surviving Spouses of Police Officers Killed in the Line of Duty BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Pound Ridge as follows: Section 1. Title. This local law shall be known as “A Local Law to Grant a Partial Real Property Tax Exemption for Surviving Spouses of Police Officers Killed in the Line of Duty” Section 2. Purpose. The purpose of this local law to grant a partial exemption from taxation of fifty percent (50%) of the assessed valuation of real property that is owned as a primary residence by the surviving spouse of a police officer who is killed in the line of duty subject to the requirements set forth in §471 of the Real Property Tax Law. Section 3. Exemption. Pursuant to Real Property Tax Law §471, the Town of Pound Ridge authorizes an exemption of fifty percent of the assessed value of qualifying real property for the surviving spouse of a police officer killed in the line of duty. Section 4. Eligibility. Such exemption shall not be granted unless: (a) the property is the primary residence of such surviving spouse (b) the conditions of New York State Real Property Tax Law §471 are met. Section 5. Application. Application for such exemption shall be filed with the Assessor on or before the taxable status date on a form as prescribed by New York State. Section 6. Severability. If any clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law shall be adjudged by and court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to said clause, sentence, paragraph, section, or part of this local law. Section 7. Effective date. This local law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the office of the Secretary of State in accordance with Municipal Home Rule Law §27. The total proposed purchase price of the 2026 Chevrolet 3500, including the snowplow package, emergency strobe lighting, and necessary equipment, is $65,684.30. Although the Ford has relatively low mileage, it is now 11 years old. Proactive replacement would help limit the risk of increasing repair costs and unexpected downtime. The Chevrolet 3500 would serve as both the Superintendent’s vehicle and an additional working truck for snow removal, storm response, roadway inspections, and daily Highway Department operations Once replaced, the Ford F-250 would be declared surplus and sold in accordance with Town procedures. I believe this is a practical investment in the Department’s reliability, flexibility, and service to the Town. text: April- The Town of East Greenbush 225 Columbia Turnpike, Rensselaer, New York 12144 TOWN BOARD AGENDA SPECIAL MEETING November 5, 2026 Call to Order Pledge of Allegiance Town Board Meeting: 6:00 PM Members of Town Board Present Absent Supervisor J. Conway Councilor H. Kennedy Councilor R. Matters Councilor J. McHugh Councilor L. Koenig Schedule of Meeting: . Open Public Privilege: NOTE – Each speaker may choose to state name and address prior to addressing the Board and shall be granted the floor for up to five minutes. The Board thanks everyone in attendance for their understanding and also for their desire to actively participate in the decision making process. All speakers must conduct themselves in a civil manner. Personal attacks will not be tolerated. Public Hearing on the 2027 Preliminary Budget 228-2026 A Resolution adopting a Proposed Local Law Creating the Position of Deputy Police Commissioner in the Town of East Greenbush WHEREAS, the Town Board received a proposed Local Law, amending Section 30-3 of the East Greenbush Code to establish within the Police Department the position of Deputy Police Commissioner, and setting forth the duties of said Deputy Police Commissioner; and WHEREAS, by a duly passed resolution the Town Board scheduled a public hearing on said proposed local law, to be held on October 28, 2026, at Town Hall; and WHEREAS, said notice of such public hearing was duly posted and published by the Town Clerk, and the public hearing was held on October 28, 2026; and WHEREAS, the Town Board wishes to go forward to adopt said proposed Local Law; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board hereby adopts the proposed Local Law creating the position of Deputy Police Commissioner in the Town of East Greenbush. 1 The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Supervisor Conway and seconded by Councilor Kennedy and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 229-2026 A Resolution to Award a Project to Provide Assessment and Planning Services to Update the Town’s Stormwater Management Program to Tighe & Bond WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 402 of the Clean Water Act (CWA), operators of small municipal separate storm sewer systems (small MS4s), located in urbanized areas, are unlawful unless they are authorized by a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit or by a state permit program. New York’s State Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (SPDES) is a NPDES-approved program with a permit issued in accordance with Environmental Conservation Law (ECL); and WHEREAS, under this permit the Town of East Greenbush is determined to be a small MS4 that is regulated under EPA's Phase II Stormwater Rule; and WHEREAS, this requires small MS4s to develop a stormwater management program (SWMP) that will reduce the amount of pollutants carried by stormwater during storm events to waterbodies to the "maximum extent practicable"; that the goal of the program is to improve water quality and recreational use of waterways; and WHEREAS, the Town is subject to certain program planning, reporting, record-keeping, and implementation requirements, including selection and implementation of minimum control measures that, when implemented together, are expected to result in a reduction of pollutants discharged into waterbodies; and WHEREAS, the Town solicited a Request For Proposals with RFP 26-07 on September 15, 2026 which requested sealed competitive bids from qualified Engineering Consultants to address the Town’s responsibility as a regulated MS4 and related requirements, including performing an assessment of the program and program planning; and WHEREAS, following the review and evaluation of all submitted proposals, the Selection Committee determined to recommend Tighe & Bond to conduct services for the performance of a comprehensive assessment of the Town’s Stormwater Management Program Plan, to draft and recommend a new Stormwater Management Program Plan in accordance with SPDES General Permit GP-0-24-001, to establish a municipal operation and facilities gap analysis, to establish a GIS system mapping review and recommendation, and to provide a comprehensive summary of SWMP recommendation; and WHEREAS, in accordance with the proposal submitted by Tighe & Bond in response to RFP 26-07, the total cost not-to-exceed to complete the proposed scope of work is $39,500.00; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance has confirmed that this resolution will have a material impact on the Town’s finances in the amount of $39,500.00; now, therefore, be it RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of East Greenbush hereby selects Tighe & Bond to conduct services required to perform an assessment and provide recommendations for 2 the drafting of a new Stormwater Management Program encompassing all requirements of GP-024-001; and be it further RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of East Greenbush authorizes the Director of Planning and Zoning to execute a Task Order Agreement between the Town of East Greenbush and Tighe & Bond to provide assessment and planning services supporting the Town’s SWMP. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor Matters and seconded by Councilor Koenig and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: 230-2026 A Resolution to Authorize the Purchase of New Servers for Town Hall and the Police Department WHEREAS, Complete Network, our contracted Information Technology (IT) provider, has recommended the replacement of servers as an urgent need for the Town; and WHEREAS, our new in-house IT Specialist has reviewed the recommendation from Complete Network and concurs that the servers must be replaced but has recommended that we go further to ensure proper licensing, fulfill our operational needs, and cut expenses in the future; and WHEREAS, SHI International Corp is under State contract for Microsoft parts (Contract # PM69723) and local government units are able to access the price in that contract; and WHEREAS, we have prepared a three-year plan for full replacement and installation of our servers, which consists of contracting with SHI International Corp on a series of one year contracts as follows:: Year One: Purchase Server CAL SLng LSA UCAL Purchase Server DC Core SLng LSA 2L Year Two: Purchase Server CAL SLng LSA UCAL Purchase server DC Core SLng LSA 2L Year Three: Purchase Server CAL SLng LSA UCAL Purchase Server DC Core SLng LSA 2L Cost: $2,651.60 Cost: $30,868.80 Total: $33,520.40 Cost: $2,651.60 Cost: $30,868.80 Total: $33,868.80 Cost: $2,651.60 Cost: $30,868.80 Total: $33,520.40 Total Cost: $100,561.20 WHEREAS, this approach will lock these costs in place, ensure proper licensing, fulfill our operational needs, and reduce costs by having prices set for three years; and WHEREAS, the Director of Finance confirms a budget amendment will be necessary from the General Fund Balance for the first year’s payment; now, therefore, be it 3 RESOLVED, that the Town Board authorizes the purchase of servers for Town Hall and the Police Department from SHI International Corp on three consecutive one-year contract for a total cost not to exceed $100,561.20. The foregoing resolution was duly moved by Councilor McHugh and seconded by Councilor Kennedy and brought to a vote resulting as follows: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: ADJOURNMENT Motion to adjourn by Supervisor Conway and seconded by Councilor Kennedy and brought to a vote as follows: Supervisor J. Conway VOTED: Councilor H. Kennedy VOTED: Councilor R. Matters VOTED: Councilor J. McHugh VOTED: Councilor L. Koenig VOTED: 4

Council consideration and discussion of a proposed local law establishing good cause eviction protections within the City of North Tonawanda, including tenant protections Explanation of Attachments: Housing Stability Law,” for Council review and consideration. Attached is the proposed Local Law Establishing Good Cause Eviction Protections within the City of North Tonawanda, titled the “North Tonawanda Tenant Protection and CITY OF NORTH TONAWANDA LOCAL LAW NO. ___ OF 2026 ALOCAL LAW ESTABLISHING GOOD CAUSE EVICTION PROTECTIONS WITHIN THE CITY OF NORTH TONAWANDA SECTION 1. TITLE This Local Law shall be known as the “North Tonawanda Tenant Protection and Housing Stability Law.” SECTION 2. LEGISLATIVE INTENT The Common Council finds that: 1. The City of North Tonawanda is a community of approximately 33,000 residents with a housing stock consisting predominantly of single-family homes, duplexes, triplexes, and four-unit residential structures. Stable housing is essential to maintaining neighborhood quality, economic vitality, and public welfare. Atthe same time, the city recognizes the importance of: o Protecting small property owners, especially those who reside in their buildings o Maintaining incentives for local investment and property maintenance Therefore, this Local Law is intended to: o Prevent unjust evictions and unreasonable rent increases o Provide clear, predictable standards o Balance tenant protections with the realities of small-scale landlords SECTION 3. DEFINITIONS 1. The term "housing accommodation’, as used in this article shall mean any residential premises, including any residential premises located within a mixed-use residential premises. 2. The term "landlord" as used in this article shall mean any fee owner, lessor, sublessor, assignor, court appointed receiver, or any other person or entity receiving or entitled to receive rent for the occupancy of any housing accommodation or an agent of any of the foregoing. 3. (a) The term "small landlord" as used in this article shall mean a landlord of no more than one (1) unit in the state 4. The term "tenant" as used in this article shall mean a tenant, sub-tenant, lessee, sublessee, or any other person entitled to the lawful possession, use or occupancy of any housing accommodation. An individual shall not be considered a tenant for the purposes of this article if: (a) no landlord-tenant relationship exists, as established pursuant to any of the grounds set forth in section 713 of the real property actions and proceedings law; or (b) the individual is an occupant, as defined in paragraph (b) of subdivision one of section 235-f of chapter 7 of the NYS real property law, who has not received the landlord's express or implied consent to use the housing accommodation as their primary residence in exchange for payment of rent. 5. The term “rent" as used in this article shall mean any consideration, including any bonus, benefit or gratuity demanded or received for or in connection with the possession, use or occupancy of housing accommodations or the execution or transfer of a lease for such housing accommodations. The term "rent" shall not include any separate charges for services, amenities or facilities which the tenant pays in addition to rent, including but not limited to charges for fitness centers, parking, storage, or facility rentals, provided that such charges are not imposed or increased for the purposes of circumventing this article. 6. The term "inflation index" shall mean five percent plus the annual percentage change in the consumer price index for all urban consumers for all items as published by the United States bureau of labor statistics for the region in which the housing accommodation is located, as established for the most recent preceding calendar year as shall be published by the division of housing and community renewal no later than the first of August in any given year. 7. The term "local rent standard" shall mean a rent increase equal to the inflation index or ten percent, whichever is lower. SECTION 4. APPLICABILITY A. Covered Units This law shall apply to: e Residential rental units within the City of North Tonawanda e Buildings containing at least two (2) dwelling units B. Exemptions The following units are exempt from this law: 1. Owner-occupied buildings with Two (2) or fewer units 2. Units subject to federal or state rent regulation programs 3. Short-term or transient occupancy (hotels, motels, etc.) SECTION 5. GOOD CAUSE REQUIRED FOR EVICTION A landlord may not remove a tenant or refuse to renew a lease unless there is good cause, including: A. The landlord is not renewing the lease because the unit is sublet and the sublessor seeks in good faith to recover possession of the unit for their own personal use and occupancy (exemption under subdivision 3 of section 214 of the Real Property Law); B. The landlord is not renewing the lease because the possession, use or occupancy of the unit is solely incident to employment, and the employment is being or has been lawfully terminated (exemption under subdivision 4 of section 214 of the Real Property Law); C. The landlord is not renewing the lease because the tenant has failed to pay rent due and owing, and the rent due or owing, or any part thereof, did not result from a rent increase which is unreasonable. A rent increase is presumptively unreasonable if the increase from the prior rent is greater than: (a) 5 percent plus the annual percentage change in the consumer price index for all urban consumers for all items as published by the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics for the region in which the housing accommodation is located, as published not later than August 1st of each year by the Division of Housing and Community Renewal; or (b) 10 percent, whichever is lower. (good cause for eviction under paragraph a of subdivision 1 of section 216 of the Real Property Law); D. The landlord is not renewing the lease because the tenant is violating a substantial obligation of their tenancy or breaching any of the tandlord's rules and regulations governing the premises, other than the obligation to surrender possession of the premises, and the tenant has failed to cure the violation after written notice that the violation must cease within 10 days of receipt of the written notice. ONLINE ACCESS: The Tentative Agenda is generally available the Friday before the meeting. The video of the meeting is usually available to watch live during the meeting. Minutes with adopted resolutions are available 1 to 2 days after the meeting. A full copy of the minutes, agenda and meeting video can be viewed on the official Town of Southold website. If you would like help navigating the site, please feel free to call my office 631-765-1800. The meeting will be accessible in person and via Zoom and streamed live on the Town’s website. A recording of the meeting will also air on Channel 1310 and will be posted on the Town’s website. Instructions and link to attend the meeting will be available on the Town’s website or by calling the Town Clerk’s office at (631)765-1800. Sincerely, Laura Byer Owner and Principal Planner laura@byerplanning.com Byer Planning, LLC 518-421-6441 Response to Town of Wilton Worth Road Multi-Use Path Feasibility Study 1 Proposed Methodology and Work Plan The Byer Planning team is comprised of organizations and individuals passionate about improving access to trail opportunities for people of all ages, abilities, and walks of life. New York State has an abundance of trail opportunities for local residents as well as those visiting from other regions, states, and countries. From the many miles of statewide trails such as the Empire State Trail and Erie Canalway Trail, to the regional connections such as the Genesee Valley Greenway and Wallkill Valley Rail Trail, and a number of other trail systems in between, there is no shortage of trail opportunities for all who live in or visit New York State. The Byer Planning team will use our experience with interactive map development as well as trail planning and implementation to develop a comprehensive scope for a future RFP for improvements to PTNY interactive maps will help all users plan out their trail visits based on their preferred activities and needs. We have outlined our proposed approach to scoping for this project below but remain flexible based on feedback from PTNY. Task 1 - Worth Road Multi-Use Path Feasibility Study (Required) Task 11 - Project Initiation and Existing Conditions Review The Byer team will develop an Existing Conditions Review of the Worth Road corridor through analysis of existing mapping, knowledge of Town staff, publicly available GIS data, and a field visit to review current conditions along the roadway. Existing conditions mapping likely to be completed includes: rights-of-way using tax parcel data; land use; topography; existing pedestrian and bicycle infrastructure; roadway characteristics such as AADT, speeds, and shoulders; and environmental constraints, such as wetlands or sensitive habitats. This information will be supplemented with an inventory of utility poles and their location throughout the corridor. ,BYER PLANNING Task 1.2 - Corridor Assessment and Constraints Analysis During the field visit and the kickoff meeting with Town Staff, the Byer team will document current opportunities and constraints along the corridor. An analysis of available right-of-way will help determine appropriate alternatives (Task 1.3). This will include a summary of existing roadway constraints, potential right-of-way acquisitions, and location of environmental features that may affect path development. In addition to challenges, this Task will summarize opportunities which support path development such as connections to key destinations and an overview of adjacent neighborhoods that would benefit from a future path along Worth Road. Task 1.3 - Conceptual Alternatives Analysis Based on the findings from Tasks 1.1 and 1.2, the Byer team will identify up to two (2) conceptual alternatives to provide a bicycle and pedestrian connection between Graphite Range Community Forest and the future Carr Road-Jones Road Multi-Use Path. These alternatives may include a variety of accommodations depending on right-of-way availability such as multi-use paths, sidewalks, on-road bicycle facilities, and/or traffic calming elements. Working with Town staff, the two alternatives will be evaluated based on connectivity, safety, environmental impacts, right- of-way considerations, constructability, and relative costs. This evaluation will help identify a preferred alternative to be further explored in Task 1.4. Task 1.4 - Preferred Alternative and Planning-Level Cost Estimate Following the Alternatives Analysis (Task 1.3), the Byer team will work with Town staff to identify a preferred alternative. The Byer team will then develop conceptual-level graphics (e.g., plan views and/or cross-sections) to visually outline the preferred alternative as well as develop a planning- level cost estimate to implement the preferred alternative. Response to Town of Wilton Worth Road Multi-Use Path Feasibility Study 2 Task 1.5 - Funding Strategy and Implementation Roadmap The Byer team will summarize public funding sources the Town may be able to utilize to fund design and construction of the future Worth Road Multi-Use Path. Additionally, the Byer team will outline a roadmap to help guide Town staff through the implementation process. This will include tasks and approximate timelines for environmental review, survey, preliminary engineering, public engagement, design, permitting, and construction.
